pr.title: Let an outer .projector.toml overrule a nearer one with [override.<priority>]
pr.head: 1845e5af23d8f11b1b2f6ee8760ce947a33cefe8

summary: Projector merges configuration from your personal file and the files above a checkout. Ordinary values favor the nearest file, which prevents a team or personal policy from changing a value the repository already commits. This layer adds explicit priority overrides without changing ordinary precedence.

An [override.1] table contains settings under their normal dotted names. Every override wins over an ordinary value; higher numbers win among overrides, and farther files break equal-priority ties. The personal file counts as farthest. Commands can edit these tables and report which priority supplied a value.

The configured gate and exact-head CI passed, together with 140 focused configuration and relay tests. The earlier key-lifecycle finding is fixed: user-only keys are ignored in every override table, including the personal file, so key removal and replacement operate on the sole effective setting.

cards.title: How a value wins
cards.html:
1. Merge ordinary settings from farthest to nearest.
  2. Apply overrides from lower to higher priority.
  3. At the same priority, apply nearer files before farther files.

cards.title: This stack layer
cards.html: The preceding layer supplies default-branch configuration reads. This layer adds overrides and their command-line editing. Destination approvals and background fetching belong to later layers.

groups.title: Apply explicit priorities after ordinary settings
groups.kicker: A shared merger decides values and their provenance
intro: An override is a setting intentionally placed above ordinary configuration. The merger first preserves the existing nearest-file rule, then sorts override tables by priority and distance. Each winning leaf records both its source file or default-branch blob and its override priority.

Only the ordinary personal file may supply agent.key, the relay private key. Overrides ignore this user-only setting, including in the personal file, so an extra copy cannot survive a key removal or outrank a replacement. Configuration commands warn about the ignored entry and can remove it explicitly.

groups.title: Edit overrides and explain the winning source
groups.kicker: The CLI exposes priority selection and source metadata
intro: Use config set or config unset with --override to change a setting inside one priority table. The existing file-scope options still select the personal, repository, or explicit file. JSON keeps the source location separate from its priority so callers do not have to parse a decorated path.
The reference documents the precedence rule and command output. The active project plan records the editor and source-format decisions settled while implementing this layer.

files.note: Parses override priorities for writes and prints priority metadata in human and JSON output.
